stem: A child arrives after a high-speed car crash with multiple injuries, hypotension and a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 7. What is the best immediate management priority?

options.text: Call the trauma team and wait for their arrival before intervening
Give morphine before assessing airway and breathing
Secure the airway with cervical spine protection and give high-flow oxygen
Log roll the child before airway assessment
Transfer directly to CT before stabilisation

explanation: A child with major trauma and a GCS of 7 needs immediate airway management with cervical spine protection as part of the primary survey. Analgesia, imaging and secondary survey steps are important but must not precede airway and oxygenation priorities.
